I've added `GET /api/admin/users/recently-created`, which returns the logins of users created in the last 7 days. I haven't built it or run any tests, as you asked.

- **Repository:** `UserRepository.findLoginsByCreatedDateAfter(Instant since)` is a JPQL query that returns only the logins, newest first.
- **Service:** `UserService.getRecentlyCreatedUserLogins()` computes `Instant.now(clock).minus(7, ChronoUnit.DAYS)` and calls the repository. This follows your Clock rule.
- **Clock bean:** The project had no `Clock` bean, so I added `config/ClockConfiguration.java`, which returns `Clock.systemUTC()`. `UserService` now takes a `Clock` in its constructor. I found no `new UserService(...)` calls in the source, so nothing else needed updating.
- **Endpoint:** In `UserResource`, `GET /users/recently-created` is protected with `@PreAuthorize` using `AuthoritiesConstants.ADMIN`, and returns the list of logins. Spring matches this literal path ahead of `/users/{login}`, so the two don't clash.

I haven't written any tests for the new endpoint. I also didn't update `notes/`, because the project has none.
